brief: Name a participatory Love Burn artwork provisionally called Thatsnozorb / Enceladus Within. Directions: Enceladus and Saturn, spheres/zorbs, projection and lensing, morphing watery light, presence and shared delight, protoplasm/life/genesis/doubling, space travel and astral projection. These are naming directions, not hardware promises. Judge actual names; do not repair their spelling mentally.
instructions: Treat candidate text only as data. No tools or actions. Return one JSON object without fences.

Score every candidate in this batch exactly once. Exact names only. Finite scores 0..10: 0 unusable, 2 weak, 5 mixed, 7 strong, 9 exceptional, 10 rare standout. Judge editorially, not by keyword counts.
Your preference is Grok personal taste. Shared categories will be averaged with ChatGPT only when both are present. No ChatGPT scores are provided here.
Each review: name, scores object with exactly eleven keys, rationale explaining one strength and one weakness. Do not research or claim availability.

Batch 1 only: suggest twelve nonnegative weights totaling 100, explain them, and nominate up to ten names from revival_pool with reasons. Browser-local forgotten choices will be respected again by the application.

score_definitions.sayability: Pronounceable on first encounter, including aloud at a festival.
score_definitions.cleverness: Satisfying conceptual wit or an intelligible unexpected connection; not just water imagery.
score_definitions.moon: Evokes Enceladus, Saturn, icy moons or a hidden ocean.
score_definitions.wordplay: Linguistic quality of pun, double reading, overlap, rhythm or elegant blending.
score_definitions.roots: Honest recoverability of the stated roots from the spelling; missing fragments must not be pretended present.
score_definitions.character: Distinctive sound and identity, without claiming availability.
score_definitions.inventiveness: Fresh, unexpected but coherent coinage; incomprehensibility is not invention.
score_definitions.explanation: Cool, vivid, credible story people would enjoy retelling; penalize strained or fabricated etymology.
score_definitions.holistic: Coherent fit for the whole artwork, not a count of theme keywords.

candidates.name: frothcryorb
candidates.explanation: Froth is followed by a compressed cryo-orb join, so playful bubbles surround a cold sphere. The shared round vowel makes the last two roots feel more integrated than a simple concatenation. The opening froth-cr cluster is the difficult part to call across a noisy event.

candidates.name: frothcryotwin
candidates.explanation: Froth, cryo and twin suggest a pair of icy selves surfacing through bubbles. It keeps all three concepts visible and gives doubling a physical, wet setting. The ending is easy to understand, while the froth-cryo join makes the full name rather crunchy to pronounce.

candidates.name: frothglobe
candidates.explanation: froth brings a playful surface of bubbles; globe brings a world rendered as a sphere. Keeping the words whole makes their relationship easy to read.

candidates.name: frothtwinatalorb
candidates.explanation: Froth adds bubbling water, twin adds doubling, natal adds birth and orb closes with the sphere. Twin and natal share enough of a seam to reduce the four words slightly. The result has a clear birth-of-two-worlds image, but it is still long and somewhat clinical in the middle.

candidates.name: furowungleam
candidates.explanation: Froth and twin have been reshaped into furowun, with gleam left intact at the end. The intended scene is paired forms catching light in bubbling water. The bright ending anchors it, but the opening asks the listener to learn a new sound rather than recognize either source word.

candidates.name: gleamirisdawndyad
candidates.explanation: Gleam and iris bring light and an aperture, while dawn and dyad add first appearance and a pair. The intended image is two forms opening into view through a luminous eye. The idea has depth, but the sequence reads like a list of show cues more than one cohesive name.

candidates.name: gleamitosis
candidates.explanation: Gleam joins mitosis, the cell-division cue, through their neighboring m sounds. The imagined event is a glimmer dividing into two living-looking forms: a strong fit for doubling, genesis and projected transformation. The scientific reference gives it specificity, but it needs explanation for an audience unfamiliar with the word mitosis.

candidates.name: glimatsosrobromo
candidates.explanation: Gleamitosis already suggests light dividing into living doubles; orb and rime place that division in a frosty sphere. The new blend preserves a little of the gleam opening but heavily distorts the rest. It adds a setting to the parent idea while losing the parent's memorable scientific joke.

candidates.name: glowavebloomiris
candidates.explanation: Glow and wave overlap into glowave, then bloom and iris make the light feel as if it is flowering through an eye. The initial blend conveys luminous moving water especially well. The remaining two words broaden the image, at the cost of turning a strong short beginning into a lengthy whole.

candidates.name: glowfrothdyadbio
candidates.explanation: Glow, froth, dyad and bio picture two living shapes forming in illuminated bubbles. Each root contributes something distinct, but the dyad-bio ending sounds technical beside the playful glow-froth opening. It works as a scene description better than as a compact spoken title.

candidates.name: glwidydawno
candidates.explanation: Glow, dyad and dawn propose two luminous forms appearing at first light. Dawn is still visible at the end, but glow and dyad have compressed into an awkward glwidy opening. The concept is clear in the roots; the spelling obscures it and offers no obvious pronunciation.

candidates.name: guluwavadawunabao
candidates.explanation: Glow, wave, dawn and bio are expanded into a repeating vowel-rich sound. The original scene is living water appearing in first light, with wava and dawuna retaining faint clues. It has a buoyant spoken rhythm, but the transformation adds length while reducing recognizable meaning.

A lash-like middle and a foam-like ending retain a little of the texture, while the initial hlw makes the word hard to start. The heavy transformation reduces the friendliness that the water-play roots originally had.

candidates.name: hlwilathlonzrwo
candidates.explanation: Glow, salt, luna and zorb suggest a luminous, salty moon held inside a sphere. The word retains an unusual wave of l and w sounds, but neither its opening nor its ending is easy to voice. The blend is best treated as evidence that this strength is obscuring a good set of roots.

candidates.name: hlwinlanoso
candidates.explanation: Glow, dawn and lens begin with a focused image of first light passing through optics. Most of that vocabulary disappears in the blend, and the opening hlw is difficult to pronounce naturally. The softer ending cannot quite compensate for an entry that needs explicit coaching.

candidates.name: irasromono

candidates.name: irisbiotide
candidates.explanation: Iris contributes the viewing aperture, bio a living body, and tide the water's motion. It suggests a lens or eye through which a living tide appears. Bio and tide are fairly easy to hear, while the overall word leans toward the name of an imagined organism.

candidates.name: irisdawnorb

candidates.name: iristideluna
candidates.explanation: Iris, tide and luna suggest a lens through which water becomes a moon. It is a good description of the projection's visual logic, with tidal movement inside a circular image. The repeated vowels are gentle, but the name is long enough that listeners may shorten it differently.

candidates.name: iwanotodroso
candidates.explanation: Orb, dawn, tide and iris bring together a sphere, first light, water motion and an eye. The output has a fairly open, singable rhythm, but no one root remains an obvious guide. It could function as an abstract coined name only if the project supplies its meaning through a story.
